t: The classic low-cost Wi-Fi chip behind countless hacked smart plugs and sensors.
steps: Buy an ESP8266 board such as a NodeMCU, D1 mini or Feather HUZZAH from a maker shop.
Get a USB cable that carries data.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Install the USB driver for clone boards with a CH340 chip.
Add the ESP8266 board package in the Arduino board manager.
Pick your board and its USB port in the menus.
Upload the Blink example and watch the light.
Try the WiFiScan example to list nearby networks.
meta: Open Board. From $9.95. A few stores.
